newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada confirms hosting Japan-Peru hostage talks.
newsitem.headline: Canada confirms hosting Japan-Peru hostage talks.

text.p: Prime Minister Jean Chretien confirmed on Wednesday Canada would host a meeting between Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on the Lima hostage crisis.
The Saturday meeting in Toronto would "discuss ways to resolve the ongoing hostage-taking in Lima," Chretien said in a statement.

Canada's ambassador to Peru, former hostage Anthony Vincent, had won respect from all sides by serving initially as a mediator after being released early in the six-week crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence.
He is also on a peace panel which it was hoped would be the forum for eventual negotiations between the Peruvian government and the leftist guerrillas holding the hostages.

"Canada has been chosen for the site of this meeting because of its role as a member of the Commission of Guarantor and the convenience of its location for both leaders," Chretien's statement said, using the panel's formal name.

Chretien spokeswoman Leslie Swartman said she expected Vincent would come up from Peru for the talks. She was not sure if Chretien would go to Toronto but pointed out the meetings would be between Fujimori and Hashimoto.
